title: Newton's law of universal gravitation
competency: Use F = Gm₁m₂/r², find g at a planet's surface and explain orbits with gravity as the centripetal force.

keywords.def: Every two masses attract with F = Gm₁m₂/r².
G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², the same everywhere in the Universe.
g = GM/R², about 9.8 m/s² at Earth's surface.
A force pulling a body toward the centre of its circle: F_c = mv²/r.

en.text: Every two masses attract each other with F = Gm₁m₂/r², where r is the distance between their centres and G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg². The force is always attractive, acts along the line joining them, and is equal and opposite on the two bodies (Newton's third law). Doubling the distance makes the force four times smaller.

am.text: ማናቸውም ሁለት ብዛቶች በ F = Gm₁m₂/r² ይሳሳባሉ። ኃይሉ ሁልጊዜ የሚስብ ነው፤ በሁለቱም ላይ እኩልና ተቃራኒ ነው።

screens.title: Switch off the Sun
screens.ask: Imagine the Sun's gravity suddenly switched off. What would the planets do?
opts: Fly off in straight lines along the tangent
screens.after:
Gravity is the only force bending the planets' paths.
With no force, Newton's first law says each planet keeps going straight at constant speed.
So each one flies off along the tangent to its orbit.
screens.best: Fly off in straight lines along the tangent

screens.title: Universal gravitation
paras: Newton saw that the force pulling an apple down also keeps the Moon in orbit.
G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², the same everywhere.
The force is always attractive, along the line joining the centres.
Each body pulls the other equally: F₁₂ = −F₂₁.

screens.title: Pull between two masses
screens.ask: Change the masses and the distance. What happens when you double r?
screens.note: Double one mass: F doubles. Double r: F becomes F/4 (inverse square).

screens.title: Key words
defs: Every two masses attract with F = Gm₁m₂/r².
G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², the same everywhere in the Universe.

screens.text: Newton's third law and gravity, true or false: a 60 kg man pulls on Earth less than Earth pulls on him.
screens.why:
F = Gm₁m₂/r² is one number for both bodies.
Newton's third law: the forces are equal and opposite.
Only the accelerations differ: a = F/m is tiny for Earth.
So the statement is false.
screens.clue: F = Gm₁m₂/r² is the same for both bodies.

screens.text: Inverse square law: two objects attract with force F. The distance between them is doubled. The new force is
screens.why:
F ∝ 1/r².
r × 2 gives F × 1/2² = F/4.
Trap: F/2 forgets to square the distance.

screens.text: Universal gravitation: Newton's law of gravitation applies to
screens.why:
The law is universal: every pair of masses attracts.
It works for apples, people, moons and stars.
The force is just tiny for small masses.

screens.ask: Gravity and mass: two spheres attract with 30 N. Each mass is doubled. The new force is ___ N
screens.why:
F ∝ m₁m₂.
Both masses ×2: F × 2 × 2 = 4F.
New force: 4 × 30 N = 120 N.
Trap: 60 N doubles only one mass.

screens.ask: Newton's law of gravitation: a 10 kg and a 100 kg mass are 1 m apart. F ≈ ___ × 10⁻⁸ N (2 decimal places)
screens.why:
Formula: F = Gm₁m₂/r².
Substitute: F = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 10 × 100 ÷ 1².
= 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 10³ = 6.67 × 10⁻⁸ N.
Answer: 6.67.

screens.ask: Newton's law of gravitation: two 2.00 kg particles are 30.0 cm apart. F ≈ ___ × 10⁻⁹ N (2 decimal places)
screens.why:
Convert: r = 30.0 cm = 0.300 m, r² = 0.0900 m².
Formula: F = Gm₁m₂/r².
Substitute: F = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 2.00 × 2.00 ÷ 0.0900.
F = 2.668 × 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 0.09 = 2.96 × 10⁻⁹ N.
Trap: using 30 instead of 0.30 m.
screens.clue: Change 30.0 cm to 0.300 m and square it.

en.text: Your weight is the gravitational pull of the planet: mg = GMm/R². Cancelling m gives g = GM/R², about 9.8 m/s² on Earth. So g does not depend on your mass; it grows with the planet's mass and falls with the square of its radius.

am.text: ክብደት የፕላኔቷ የስበት ኃይል ነው፡ mg = GMm/R²፤ ስለዚህ g = GM/R² ≈ 9.8 m/s²። g በሰውዬው ብዛት አይወሰንም።

screens.title: A bigger Earth
screens.ask: Suppose Earth kept its mass but swelled to 8 times its volume. Your weight would become
screens.after:
Volume ∝ R³, so 8 times the volume means R doubles (2³ = 8).
Weight = GMm/R² ∝ 1/R².
R × 2 gives weight × 1/4.
The trap is 1/8: it uses volume instead of radius.

screens.title: Where g comes from
paras: So mg = GM_E m/R_E², and g = GM_E/R_E².

screens.title: Design a planet
screens.ask: Change the planet's mass and radius (Earth = 1). Watch g.
outs: Weight of a 60 kg student, mg
screens.note: Earth: g = 9.8 m/s², weight 588 N. Mass up: g up. Radius up: g down by R².

screens.title: Key word
defs: g = GM/R², about 9.8 m/s² at Earth's surface.

screens.text: Surface gravity and mass: Earth keeps its size but has one-third of its mass. Your weight becomes
screens.why:
Weight W = GMm/R².
Same R, so W ∝ M.
M × 1/3 gives W × 1/3.

screens.ask: Weight from Newton's law: M_E = 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, R_E = 6.38 × 10⁶ m. The pull on a 60.0 kg person is ≈ ___ N (nearest newton)
screens.why:
Formula: F = GM_E m/R_E².
R_E² = (6.38 × 10⁶)² = 4.07 × 10¹³ m².
F = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 5.97 × 10²⁴ × 60.0 ÷ 4.07 × 10¹³.
Result: F ≈ 587 N.
Check: mg = 60 × 9.8 = 588 N ✓ (the book prints 584 N).
screens.clue: Use F = GMm/R², or check with mg.

screens.ask: Surface gravity: a planet has 4 times Earth's mass and twice its radius. g there = ___ m/s²
screens.why:
g = GM/R², so g ∝ M/R².
M × 4 and R × 2: g × 4/2² = g × 1.
g = 9.8 m/s², the same as Earth.

screens.text: Free fall, true or false: a heavy stone and a light stone fall with the same g (no air resistance).
screens.why:
Set mg = GMm/R².
The stone's mass m cancels on both sides.
g = GM/R² does not depend on the stone.
So both fall with the same g: true.

screens.ask: Surface gravity: a planet has twice Earth's mass and half its radius. g there = ___ m/s²
screens.why:
g ∝ M/R².
M × 2, R × ½: g × 2/(½)² = g × 2 × 4 = 8g.
g = 8 × 9.8 = 78.4 m/s².
Trap: 2 × 2 = 4 forgets to square the ½.

en.text: A body moving in a circle needs a centripetal force F_c = mv²/r toward the centre. For planets this force is the Sun's gravity: GMₛ m/r² = mv²/r, so v² = GMₛ/r. With v = 2πr/T this gives T²/r³ = 4π²/(GMₛ), which is Kepler's third law with K ≈ 2.97 × 10⁻¹⁹ s²/m³.

am.text: በክብ የሚንቀሳቀስ አካል ወደ መሀል የሚስብ ኃይል mv²/r ያስፈልገዋል፤ ለፕላኔቶች ይህ የፀሐይ ስበት ነው። ከዚህ T²/r³ = 4π²/(GM) ይገኛል።

screens.title: Why don't planets fall in?
screens.ask: The Sun pulls every planet. Why don't the planets fall into the Sun?
opts: They move sideways fast enough to keep curving round it
Gravity does not reach that far
screens.after:
The Sun pulls each planet toward it.
But the planet also moves sideways very fast.
The pull only bends its path into a curve: it keeps "falling" round the Sun.
screens.best: They move sideways fast enough to keep curving round it

screens.title: Centripetal force
paras: A force toward the centre of a circle is a centripetal force.
For planets, the Sun's gravity supplies it.
Earth's gravity does the same for the Moon and satellites.
Without it, a planet would go straight on.

screens.title: Put a satellite in orbit
screens.ask: Move the orbit radius (from Earth's centre). Gravity is the centripetal force.
screens.note: Farther out: slower and a longer period. At r ≈ 42 200 km, T ≈ 24 h: the satellite keeps pace with Earth's spin.

screens.title: Kepler's third law from Newton
steps: Gravity = centripetal force: GMₛ m/r² = mv²/r.
Cancel m and one r: v² = GMₛ/r.

screens.title: Key word
defs: A force pulling a body toward the centre of its circle: F_c = mv²/r.

screens.text: Centripetal force in orbits: what supplies the centripetal force that keeps Earth in orbit?
screens.why:
A circle needs a force toward its centre.
The centre of Earth's orbit is (near) the Sun.
The Sun's gravity pulls Earth that way.
So the Sun's gravity is the centripetal force.

screens.text: Orbital speed: from v² = GMₛ/r, planets closer to the Sun move
screens.why:
v² = GMₛ/r: r is in the denominator.
Smaller r gives larger v².
So closer planets move faster (Mercury is faster than Earth).

screens.ask: Mass of the Sun from Earth's orbit: T = 3.156 × 10⁷ s, r = 1.496 × 10¹¹ m. Mₛ ≈ ___ × 10³⁰ kg (2 decimal places)

screens.text: Kepler's constant for satellites: for satellites of Earth, the constant in T²/r³ = K is
screens.why:
K = 4π²/(GM), where M is the central body.
For Earth's satellites the central body is Earth.
So K = 4π²/(GM_E).
Trap: 2.97 × 10⁻¹⁹ s²/m³ is the Sun's value.
screens.clue: Which body is at the centre?

screens.ask: Period from Newton's law: Mercury orbits at 5.8 × 10¹⁰ m; Mₛ = 1.99 × 10³⁰ kg. Its period ≈ ___ Earth days (nearest day)
screens.clue: Use T² = 4π²r³/(GMₛ), then divide seconds by 86 400.

test.ask: Newton's law of gravitation: two 1 kg masses are 1 m apart. F = ___ × 10⁻¹¹ N
test.why:
F = Gm₁m₂/r² = G × 1 × 1 ÷ 1².
So F = G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N.

test.text: Inverse square law: the distance between two masses is tripled. The force becomes
test.why:
F ∝ 1/r².
r × 3 gives F × 1/3² = F/9.
Trap: F/3 forgets the square.

test.text: Gravity with two changes: both masses are doubled and the distance is doubled. The force becomes
test.why:
F ∝ m₁m₂/r².
Masses: × 2 × 2 = × 4.
Distance: × 1/2² = × 1/4.
Total: 4 × 1/4 = 1, so the force stays F.

test.text: Direction of gravity, true or false: the gravitational force between two masses can be repulsive.
test.why:
Gravity always pulls masses together.
It is never a push.
So the statement is false.

test.ask: Surface gravity: a planet has Earth's radius but twice its mass. g = ___ m/s²
test.why:
g = GM/R²; same R, so g ∝ M.
g = 2 × 9.8 = 19.6 m/s².

notes.text: Example 2.21: 6.673 × 10⁻¹¹ × 5.97 × 10²⁴ × 60/(6.38 × 10⁶)² = 587 N, not 584 N (agrees with mg = 588 N). The blank accepts 587 and 588.
Figure 2.22 labels both forces F₂₁; one should be F₁₂. The text uses G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ and the examples 6.673 × 10⁻¹¹; answers agree.
p.62: "speed of the plane" means planet; K ≈ 2.97 × 10⁻¹⁹ needs the unit s²/m³. Exercise 2.5 Q3 option B "Plants" means planets.
